title: QCon London 2027 Announces 15 Tracks on Production AI, Architecture, and Engineering at Scale
gist: Promotional announcement of QCon London 2027 (April 13-16, QEII Centre): 15 tracks and 75+ practitioner speakers, with the program weighted toward production agentic AI (eval platforms, guardrails, agent security) next to established architecture, distributed systems and Staff+ topics. Early-bird ticket is £2,290; with the ICSAET certification workshop it is £2,800.

themes.theme: Agent productionization as the dominant practitioner agenda

insights.claim: QCon London 2027 gives dedicated tracks to eval platforms and guardrails for agentic AI and to protecting systems from both humans and autonomous agents. This signals that taking agents from prototype to production is now a mainstream engineering concern.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Agent evaluation and guardrail tooling is becoming a recognized spending category for enterprise engineering teams.
insights.quote: Moving an agent from a prototype into production requires teams to define acceptable behavior, test changing outputs, enforce boundaries

insights.claim: The organizers' view is that no single universal guardrail architecture exists for agents. Controls have to be divided across models, applications, platforms and operational processes, and gaps can remain.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: The AI safety-tooling market is likely to stay fragmented across layers instead of consolidating into one guardrail product.
insights.quote: The aim is not to find one universal guardrail architecture, but to understand which controls address which risks and where gaps can remain.

themes.theme: AI's second-order effects on architecture and delivery

insights.claim: Adding AI to existing systems introduces probabilistic outputs, new dependencies and new data flows, and these have to be integrated without weakening reliability, operability, security or changeability.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: AI integration raises demand for reliability and observability spending, not only model spending.
insights.quote: Adding AI to an existing system introduces new dependencies, probabilistic outputs, data flows, and scaling characteristics.
insights.locator: Deciding what architecture and delivery practices

insights.claim: Production trade-offs interact: a throughput gain can make debugging harder, and AI-oriented data platforms can create new operational dependencies.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Infrastructure investment for AI carries hidden operational costs that buyers tend to underestimate.
insights.quote: A throughput improvement may make debugging harder. A data platform designed for AI workloads may create new operational dependencies.
insights.locator: These concerns cannot be evaluated independently

insights.claim: QCon London 2027 runs April 13-15 at the QEII Centre with a certification workshop on April 16 led by Luca Mezzalira. Early-bird tickets are £2,290 and conference plus certification is £2,800 through October 13.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Premium practitioner conferences are adding certifications to raise revenue per attendee.
insights.quote: Early-bird conference tickets are £2,290 through October 13. Conference and certification tickets are £2,800 through October 13.
